parties:
Golam Mohammad ----- Appellant.
Vs.
Sree Sailendra Nath Kanangoe being dead his heirs Sree Biman Behari Kanangoe and others ----- Respondents.
full_judgment: 5. On the second point Mr. Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, learned Counsel for the appellant, has taken us through sections 23 and 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act which were not placed before this Court while disposing of CP No. 10 of 1974. Section 23 provides that in case of transfer of pre-emptible non-agricultural land the pre-emptor has to file notices together with process fees for service thereof on all co-sharer tenants who are not parties to the transfer. Section 24 provides that within 4 months of the service of notice or within 4 months from the date of knowledge of such transfer, if no notice has been issued or served, a co-sharer may apply to the Court for pre-emption. From all these provisions in sections 23 and 24 of the Act Mr. Ahmed submits that although no specific provision has been made requiring a pre-emptor to make all co-sharers as parties, as has been done by section 96(2) in the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, it is imperative that the co-sharer-tenants must be made parties to an application under section 24 of the Act to give meaning and validity to the provision of service of notice of transfer to them and to the provision of their choice of pre-emption. Failure to add one of the co-sharers as a party will result in the failure of the application on the ground of defect of party, he submits. He further submits that the express provision of adding all co-sharer-tenants in an application under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act was necessary because priorities have to be fixed in respect of pre-emption between co-sharers of various types and contiguous owners, but in respect of pre-emption under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act only the co-sharers can apply for pre-emption and there is no provision for fixation of priority among them. As such no specific provision was made in the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act requiring co-sharers to be added as parties. He also submits that in the absence of any provision as to who may be added as parties in a proceeding under section 24, the procedural law, namely, Order I, rule 3 and Order I rule 10(2) CPC will govern the field.
